review.notes: Era mismatch on the display text. v0 (IOC-020) lacks the sentence 'This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set.' that v1 (SD4-EN008, 2005-05-09) added, and v2 (DR2-EN020, 2005-10-20) - the text the GOAT variant ships verbatim - only reshuffles v1's wording ('removing from play 2 WATER monsters' for 'removing 2 WATER monsters ... from play', 'their' for 'his/her'). No behavioural consequence is demonstrable from the packet: neither script registers any Normal Summon restriction (both are c:EnableReviveLimit() plus EFFECT_SPSUMMON_PROC from the hand, the prohibition being carried by the card's cdb type rather than by Lua), and apart from the trigger event and | vs + constant spelling the two scripts are identical. Recorded as an era mismatch of the period text rather than as a functional change, because the packet gives no script evidence either way for the v0 -> v1 sentence. Forward from the baseline, v2 -> v3 (IOC-EN020, Invasion of Chaos 25th Anniversary Edition, 2023-04-20) reverts to the v1 wording, which is exactly what the pinned modern cdb text matches - a trailing cosmetic transition, recorded here rather than as a change entry. The battle-destruction timing is a per-card ruling because no rule-profile flag can redirect a card to a different event code.

event.historical_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 2 WATER monsters in your Graveyard. When this card destroys an opponent's monster as a result of battle, your opponent skips their next Draw Phase.
event.summary: Era trigger timing, not a text erratum: the GOAT script registers the mandatory 'your opponent skips their next Draw Phase' trigger on EVENT_BATTLED with its own condition (GetBattleTarget() is the opponent's and IsBattleDestroyed()), where the modern script uses EVENT_BATTLE_DESTROYING with aux.bdocon at the instant of destruction. Upstream annotates the variant 'Battle destroyed registers while the mosnter is on field'. Chronology unresolved - nothing in the packet or in chronologies.json bounds it.
